chunks: Abu Basir asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about thunder: what does it say?
He said: “It is like a man who is among the camels and drives them on, saying, ‘Hai, Hai,’ something like that.”
He said: I said, “May I be your ransom, then what is the case of lightning?”
So he said: “Those are the whips of the angels; they strike the clouds and drive them to the place in which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has decreed the rain.”

key_terms.الرَّعْدِ: thunder, discussed here as a sound likened to a driver’s call
key_terms.السَّحَابَ: the clouds that are driven to their appointed place
key_terms.الْبَرْقِ: lightning, described as an instrument used by the angels
key_terms.الْمَطَرَ: the rain sent to the place appointed by Allah
key_terms.الْمَلَائِكَةِ: the angels, who are described as directing the clouds by Allah’s command

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام say about the meaning of thunder and lightning?
ai.summary: This hadith describes thunder and lightning as part of the divine ordering of natural phenomena. Thunder is likened to the driving call used with camels, while lightning is described as the angels’ instruments for driving the clouds to the place where Allah has decreed rain.
